reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports galvanic corrosion between FCC and σ phases in CoCrFeNiMo and that oxide films form and rupture during wear, but it does not address the key premise that galvanic coupling causes uneven/unstable oxide formation, nor does it cover the synergistic acceleration under simultaneous wear–corrosion at elevated temperature.
premises: Multi-phase HEA has phases with dissimilar electrochemical potentials
Galvanic coupling occurs at phase boundaries
Galvanic coupling leads to uneven/unstable oxide film formation
Mechanical wear ruptures the unstable oxide film
Ruptured film exposes fresh surfaces, accelerating both corrosion and wear
